items.plain: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer let an attacker on the network run code on the device without logging in; patch or apply Fortinet's workaround now.
items.summary: An output-encoding flaw in the JSON RPC API of FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer lets an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code or commands via a specially crafted HTTP request when the JSON API is enabled. Fortinet's November advisories cover the 7.6 and 8.0 lines — patch now, or apply workarounds where a fix is still upcoming.

items.plain: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer let an attacker on the network run commands on the device without logging in; upgrade to a fixed version now.
items.summary: A SQL injection flaw in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer lets an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the OFTP port run code or commands on the system via crafted OFTP packets. Fortinet's November advisories cover affected 7.2 through 8.0 releases — upgrade to a fixed version.

items.plain: Puppet lets an attacker with a signed agent certificate run code on the central server; upgrade Puppet now, and check certificate signing.
items.summary: A deserialization flaw in Puppet's report-processing code lets a client holding any CA-signed agent certificate run arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 18 November citing active exploitation — upgrade Puppet Core to 8.22.2 or 9.1.3, or Puppet Enterprise to a fixed release.

items.plain: Puppet Enterprise lets an attacker with a crafted certificate impersonate other servers; upgrade Puppet Enterprise now.
items.summary: A certificate-name matching flaw in Puppet Server's authorization lets a client whose certificate name extends or shortens an authorized hostname be authorized as that host, enabling impersonation of other nodes and, in Puppet Enterprise, access to certificate-authority administration. Upgrade to a fixed Puppet Enterprise release.

items.plain: OpenMage lets an attacker trick a logged-in shop admin into approving a malicious request; upgrade OpenMage now.
items.summary: A cross-site request forgery flaw in OpenMage Magento LTS's OAuth confirm actions lets an attacker holding OAuth consumer credentials trick a logged-in administrator or customer into authorizing the attacker's request. Upgrade to 20.18.2 or 21.0.0-beta3.
